CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney stone with severe pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports pain that started approximately three days ago in the left back. Pain is constant and has been traveling lower but stone has not yet passed. Patient reports inability to get comfortable. This is patient's third kidney stone episode. Patient has been able to urinate and noted blood in urine this morning. Patient denies fever but reports some chills, nausea, and inability to eat due to pain. Patient has attempted pain management with Tylenol and ibuprofen without significant relief. Previous kidney stone episodes typically resolved in three to four days.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies fever, chest pain, and abdominal pain. Patient reports chills, nausea, and pain radiating from left back into groin. Patient reports hematuria.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes mellitus, prior kidney stones (two previous episodes), systolic ejection murmur grade 2 out of 6.

MEDICATIONS
Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension, metformin 500 mg for diabetes, Tylenol as needed, ibuprofen as needed for pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports difficulty limiting salt intake and enjoys french fries.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: Grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur noted. Lungs: Clear bilaterally, no crackles or wheezes. Abdomen: Tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. CVA tenderness on the right flank.

RESULTS
Blood pressure on today's visit: elevated, likely due to pain. Patient's home blood pressure readings typically in 130s-140s with one reading of 150; diastolic 70-80. Pre-meal blood glucose readings in low 100s. Previous glucose test couple of months ago was around 300. A1c at last visit: 7.3.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Suspected kidney stone with costovertebral angle tenderness and inflammation. Plan includes: (1) Prescribe oxycodone 5 mg every 6 to 8 hours as needed for pain; continue Tylenol for breakthrough pain. (2) Increase fluid intake to promote stone passage. (3) Provide urine strainer to catch stone if passed. (4) Referral to urology even if stone passes to address recurrent kidney stone formation. (5) Continue Norvasc 2.5 mg for hypertension; blood pressures adequate on current dose. (6) Continue metformin 500 mg for diabetes. (7) Referral to dietitian/nutrition for dietary counseling and salt reduction to 2300 mg daily to help manage hypertension and diabetes.
